**Finding repaired and submitted: Deviation (narrow, duration only).**

The substance of Section 19 remains strong, so I kept the edit to the one parameter that falls short of the preferred position and that also triggered the deterministic period check.

**Redline (validated, ok:true) — § 19.2 / p0072**
> For ~~ninety days~~ **twelve (12) months** after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria.

**Comment:** [Playbook] We have extended the Deliverable conformity warranty in 19.2 from ninety days to twelve (12) months, since Deliverables include software, configurations and integrations whose defects typically surface over a full operating cycle; our playbook position is 12 months for software and 90 days for services. The remedy in 19.4 is unchanged, and we can accept ninety (90) days as a fallback if the longer period is not workable.

**Why this and nothing more:**
- 19.1 (professional and workmanlike + material conformity), 19.3 (Applicable Law, no malicious code, no functionality diminution) and 19.4 (re-perform/repair/replace → termination and refund, non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims) already satisfy the rule.
- 19.5 is confined to implied warranties and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and remedies, so no disclaimer carve-out is needed.
- Hosted Services conformity for the whole subscription term already exceeds the 12-month software benchmark; only the Deliverable period sat at the fallback level, and the numerals now also remove the phrasing ambiguity.
